$comment: Configuration of the SEO pulse for internal-agents.com. One site, one catalog, pages generated from templates. Edit this file to add or remove tracked terms, route families, or impression sinks.
$comment_tracked_keywords: The demand space of the catalog: how organizations build agents for their own teams, and the work those agents do. Volumes are cheap, so this set is wider than the set worth tracking positions for.
$comment_rank_keywords: Terms the catalog can realistically hold a position for. Head terms such as 'agentic ai' or 'claude code' belong to vendors and news sites, so tracking them spends credits for no signal. The ownable shapes are the catalog's own subject (an organization with a named system) and the questions the catalog answers directly.
rank_keywords: how companies build internal ai agents
$comment_route_families: Every page comes from a template, so a defect is normally a family defect, not a page defect. The audit reads routing-manifest.json, sorts each route into the first family whose pattern matches, and reports by family. `jsonld_types` are the @type values the family's graph must carry beyond the shared Organization and WebSite nodes. `min_words` is the floor for the words of the main element, set below the family today, so that it reports a loss of content and not the normal size of the page.
$comment_page_rules: Shared limits for the head of every page. The titles carry the ' · Internal Agents Map' suffix, so the title limit includes it. og_image_default names the shared card; a page other than the home page that still points at it has fallen back to the default preview.
$comment_query_rules: Rules for the Search Console queries export (gsc-queries.mjs). `brand_pattern` separates searches for the site itself from searches for its subject. Striking distance is the position band where a title or description change on the page that already appears is the cheapest move on the site.
$comment_impression_sinks: Pages that collect large numbers of impressions at near-zero click-through, so they move every site-level number away from what the catalog pages do. They are excluded from the 'ex-sinks' view of the search-performance report, never from the site total. The list starts empty: the Markdown twins (`/agents/<id>.md`), `/llms.txt`, and `/agents.json` are the candidates to watch, because they answer machine requests and humans do not click them. Add a page here once it behaves that way, and remove it when it stops.
$comment_competitors: Sites that answer the same questions. Watch them in the drift phase, not in the scripts.

paths.$comment: Run the scripts from the repository root. Snapshots are regenerable state that Git ignores; reports are history and get committed.
